body:
This continues to be an issue on OS X as of a commit from a week ago (I can try again with the latest master). It has been reported previously in #100.

**Edit:** Confirmed to occur with current master 22c5192b3d268d86533ed703ed3ae9c4ad59883b. OS X 10.9.2 (latest public release). It happens with `./tests/clipboard` program, exactly as described in https://github.com/glfw/glfw/issues/100#issuecomment-21386487.

Strange, the programs in `./tests/` folder seem to have the bug as described above (i.e. cursor becomes hidden while over the window after a resize). However, apps in `./examples/` (e.g., Boing.app, Gears.app, etc.) appear to have the cursor in GLFW_CURSOR_HIDDEN mode from the start (i.e. no resize necessary).

It feels that the relevant factor is whether the app is launched from the terminal (as in the case of `./tests/*`) or from Finder (the case for `./examples/*.app`).
@shurcooL Can't confirm that. The examples and tests behave the same way on my machine.

Which way is that? What OS X version are you running? Which commit did you try.

**Edit:** I just tried it on a another MacBook with OS X 10.9.2, same thing. It's definitely the .app bundle vs. binary. All I'm doing:

``` bash
git clone https://github.com/glfw/glfw.git
cd ./glfw
git checkout 9209d9b30444e996dff847f985d6684a9b40001c

cmake .
make
```

Interesting. Have you tried moving mouse cursor out and back over the window (for .app bundles, that's what makes the cursor hidden before any resizes for me)?

Perhaps it's something in my `~/.profile` that's creating the discrepancy. I can't think of much else.

The cursor stays visible for me until I resize the window. It becomes visible again when I focus another window and then switch back.

`src/cocoa_window.m` is pretty straight forward. ~~I'm starting to think this is a bug inside Cocoa.~~
Apple provides a simple [OpenGL example app](https://developer.apple.com/library/mac/samplecode/GLEssentials/Introduction/Intro.html) that doesn't have this issue. They're using NSOpenGLView though, so I'm not sure it's helpful.
I noticed that with the GLFW version 3.0.4 downloaded from the website i don't have this issue.

@EncryptedSoul @elmindreda  Can't believe I missed that! I also can't believe that I haven't found the bug earlier given that [it's documented](https://github.com/glfw/glfw/blob/master/src/cocoa_window.m#L671-L672) ... Anyway here's the commit that first introduced it: 8ae063bb1b61cf0daa9c4d4c10d6a189e8cad121

Edit: The NSView and NSWindow docs suggest we probably shouldn't be calling `discardCursorRects`. I'm not entirely sure how the cursor is related to the drag and drop code. Does anybody know? Is the cursor supposed to be hidden when a file is dragged onto the window?
Yep, I can't believe I forgot to check it too, but I can confirm the bug was not present in 3.0.4. So it's the drag-and-drop stuff that broke it.

I can confirm this error too. In particular, this happens when I resize the window, then move the window to another screen (from retina to non-retina or vice versa; didn't try with two non-retina screens).
Hey, I solved the issue by simply comment the discardCursorRects function and now it works fine to me.
